Caption / description / post text:
101 Steak and Potato Variations Pt. 2: Creamy Steak Gnocchi 🥩🥔   Servings: 4-5 Total time: 50–55 minutes Ingredients: ~24oz top sirloin or thin-cut NY strips (12oz in the soup, 12oz for garnish) 1 package potato gnocchi (16–18 oz) 2 tbsp olive oil 1 onion, diced 3–4 garlic cloves, minced 1 Tbsp sun dried tomatoes 4–5 sprigs thyme 1 cup white wine 4 cups beef stock 3 cups chopped kale Cornstarch slurry (2 Tbsp cornstarch + 2 Tbsp cold water 1 cup heavy cream ½–1 cup grated Parmesan Salt + pepper Instructions: -Heat the olive oil in a pot or Dutch oven over medium heat. Add the diced onion and sauté for 4–5 minutes, stirring occasionally, until softened and translucent. Add the minced garlic and sun-dried tomatoes and cook for another 1–2 minutes, until fragrant -Pour in the white wine and use a wooden spoon to scrape up any browned bits from the bottom of the pot. Bring to a gentle simmer and cook for 3–5 minutes, or until the wine has reduced by about half -Add the beef stock and thyme sprigs. Bring to a gentle simmer and cook uncovered until the broth has reduced by about half, allowing the flavors to concentrate -While the broth simmers, cook the steaks in a separate skillet or grill until they reach your desired doneness. Transfer the steaks to a cutting board and let them rest for 5–10 minutes before slicing. Reserve half of the steak for the soup and half for topping. -Pour any juices released from the resting steaks into the gnocchi (if desired). Stir in the chopped kale and cook for 2–3 minutes, until it begins to wilt. Add the gnocchi and cook according to the package directions, until tender (about 3-4 minutes) -Stir in the cornstarch slurry and simmer for 1–2 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the broth thickens slightly. -Remove the thyme sprigs, then reduce the heat to low. Stir in the heavy cream and Parmesan. Season with salt and pepper to taste, keeping the broth at a gentle heat and avoiding a hard boil -Ladle into bowls and top with the reserved steak. Serve warm with additional Parmesan and freshly cracked black pepper

Transcript of the video's audio (machine-made):
Welcome to 101 ways to make steak and potatoes. Second on the list, creamy steak gnocchi. Mmm, gotta be kidding me. I can't believe I just made that. Whip out your Dutch oven and throw in onions, garlic, and sun-dried tomatoes with white cooking wine until reduced by half. Add in the beef stock in time and let's get on with the steak. I went with some choice-cut New York strips that will be cooking over the coals. It'll take the flavors in this dish to an insane level. Once the broth is reduced a bit, mixing kale, gnocchi, cornstarch, slurry, heavy cream, and parmesan until it's creamy like this. At this point, the steaks are rested and so juicy. You don't have to cut them this tall, but it is fun. Peace them out and launch into that creamy gnocchi for a bite you'll never forget.
